Prokinetic drugs such as metoclopramide, or erythromycin, have been used to promote gastric emptying and reduce residual gastric volumes.7-9 Complexation of the nutrients with aluminium-containing antac- ids, also given via the tube, may occur and this deposition of sol- id masses may cause oesophageal obstruction.10 Diarrhoea in patients receiving enteral nutrition may not neces- sarily be caused by the tube feeding itself;11,12 malabsorption, in- fections and microbial contamination, underlying disease, and concomitant drug therapy can be possible contributors.1,2,4,13,14 However, enteral feeding has been shown to be associated with increased colonic secretion, which can be reversed by infusion of short-chain fatty acids.15 Because colonic microflora may play a role in the pathogenesis of diarrhoea associated with enteral feeds, manipulation of the microflora using pre- or probiotics has been suggested as a means of reducing the incidence, duration or severity thereof, and some enteral feeding formulas contain pre- biotics. However, few studies have investigated the effect on di- arrhoea, and further research is warranted.14 While enteral tube feeding and the presence of a nasogastric tube are risk factors for infection, optimal nourishment through enter- al feeding in high-risk patients unable to tolerate oral nutrition may also improve their immune status.16 1.
